To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the propagation of calcium waves in mouse neuroblastoma is limited by local diffusion of calcium and that this diffusion is rapid and is not slowed by cytoplasmic buffers.
calcium acting in positive feedback diffuses in the cytoplasm of neuroblastoma cells at nearly the rate of free diffusion, and that this occurs within the first 0.l ms after a Ca2+ channel opens.

the local positive feedback of calcium in the propagation is due to rapid diffusion of calcium in the first 1/5 of a micron after release from an internal store, and that this occurs within the first 1.6 ms after release, which is the time for calcium release to spread from a single channel to neighboring channels.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the propagation of calcium waves in neuroblastoma cells.
the propagation of intracelular calcium waves.

the propagation of intracelluar calcium waves, and we have found that calcium diffusion from an open calcium release channel to neighboring release channels is a rate-determinng regenerative step in the propagation of these waves.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
local positive feedback by Ca2+ diffusion is a key mechanism in the propagation of waves of intracellular Ca2+.
local positive feedback by diffusion of calcium is the rate-limiting step in the propagation of calcium waves in mouse neuroblastoma.
calcium diffusion in cytoplasm is a local positive feedback mechanism that is important in the propagation of calcium waves.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calcium diffusion from an open calcium channel to neighboring calcium release sites is, in this system, a rate-limiting regenerative step.
calcium release is propagated by a local positive feedback mechanism in which calcium diffusing from an open release channel activates neighboring release channels.
the calcium wave propagation is a local positive feedback by calcium.
The main takeaway from our work is that
calcium diffusion from a channel to a neighboring channel is an important rate-determining step in calcium wavefront propagation.
calcium waves are not simply the result of diffusion, but are a result of local positive feedback by calcium.
the propagation of intracelular calcium waves is limited by local positive feedback.
